caption.en: The title page of Hollis Dann's Fourth Year Music (New York, 1916), a school music book he compiled while professor of music at Cornell University: the book that holds the round's earliest known printing.
caption.es: La portada de Fourth Year Music, de Hollis Dann (Nueva York, 1916), un libro escolar de música que compiló siendo profesor de música en la Universidad Cornell: el libro que guarda la primera impresión conocida del canon.

alt.en: Printed music headed "MAY BELLS" and "ROUND": two staves in 4/4 with three flats, the first marked I and the second II, with the words "1. White coral bells upon a slender stalk" and "2. Oh, don't you wish that you could hear them ring?" under the first, and "Lilies of the valley deck our garden walk." and "That could happen only when the fairies sing." under the second.
alt.es: Música impresa con el título "MAY BELLS" y "ROUND": dos pentagramas en 4/4 con tres bemoles en la clave, el primero marcado I y el segundo II, con la letra "1. White coral bells upon a slender stalk" y "2. Oh, don't you wish that you could hear them ring?" bajo el primero, y "Lilies of the valley deck our garden walk." y "That could happen only when the fairies sing." bajo el segundo.

caption.en: "May Bells", headed "Round", on page 115 of Fourth Year Music (1916), the round's earliest known printing: for two voices, the second, marked II, coming in at the fifth bar, with no author or composer named.
caption.es: "May Bells", con el encabezado "Round", en la página 115 de Fourth Year Music (1916), la primera impresión conocida del canon: para dos voces, la segunda, marcada II, entra en el quinto compás, y no se nombra autor ni compositor.

source: Hollis Dann, Fourth Year Music, Hollis Dann Music Course (New York: American Book Company, 1916), p. 115, "May Bells", Round (cropped to the round)

alt.en: A coloured botanical print inside a pink ruled border: a lily of the valley with three broad dark-green leaves, a slender stalk hung on one side with small white bell-shaped flowers, and the root at the foot; engraved below are "Lilium Convallium, album. T. 77.", "Ital. Mughetto, o Fioraliso" and "Gall. Muguet", with "Magdalena Bouchard sculp." at the right and "5." in the top corner.
alt.es: Un grabado botánico coloreado dentro de un marco rosa: un lirio de los valles con tres hojas anchas de color verde oscuro, un tallo delgado del que cuelgan a un lado pequeñas flores blancas en forma de campana, y la raíz al pie; debajo, grabado, "Lilium Convallium, album. T. 77.", "Ital. Mughetto, o Fioraliso" y "Gall. Muguet", con "Magdalena Bouchard sculp." a la derecha y "5." en la esquina superior.

caption.en: A lily of the valley in a coloured etching by Magdalena Bouchard, printed in Rome in 1772: its small white bells hang in a row along a slender stalk, the "white coral bells upon a slender stalk" of the round's first line.
caption.es: Un lirio de los valles en un aguafuerte coloreado de Magdalena Bouchard, impreso en Roma en 1772: sus pequeñas campanas blancas cuelgan en fila a lo largo de un tallo delgado, las "white coral bells upon a slender stalk" (campanas de coral blanco sobre un tallo delgado) del primer verso del canon.

source: Lily-of-the-valley (Convallaria majalis L.): entire flowering plant. Coloured etching by M. Bouchard, 1772 (Rome: Bouchard et Gravier) (cropped to the plate's border)
licenceEvidence: Wellcome Collection catalogue record (api.wellcomecollection.org/catalogue/v2/works/jzpwuffs): image licence "Public Domain Mark"; etching with watercolour, Rome, 1772, by Magdalena Bouchard, with Giorgio Bonelli (see rights.md).

alt.en: A printed paragraph from a preface: "ROUNDS. Children who are inexperienced will find difficulty in singing one part while listening to another. Part singing is an ear problem as well as a sight reading one. Rounds are especially useful in developing the power to sing 'in the presence of' another melody. The Round should be sung again and again as a unison song until the children are thoroughly familiar with it; then it may be attempted as a Round."
alt.es: Un párrafo impreso de un prefacio: "ROUNDS. Children who are inexperienced will find difficulty in singing one part while listening to another. Part singing is an ear problem as well as a sight reading one. Rounds are especially useful in developing the power to sing 'in the presence of' another melody. The Round should be sung again and again as a unison song until the children are thoroughly familiar with it; then it may be attempted as a Round."

caption.en: From Dann's preface to Fourth Year Music (1916): rounds, he tells teachers, build the power to sing "in the presence of" another melody, and each should be sung in unison until the children know it well.
caption.es: Del prefacio de Dann a Fourth Year Music (1916): los cánones, explica a los maestros, desarrollan la capacidad de cantar "en presencia de" otra melodía, y cada uno debe cantarse al unísono hasta que los niños lo conozcan bien.

source: Hollis Dann, Fourth Year Music, Hollis Dann Music Course (New York: American Book Company, 1916), Preface, p. 6, paragraph "Rounds" (cropped to that paragraph)
